newsitem.title: UK: Euro low sulphur fuel slips on talk of cargo deals.
newsitem.headline: Euro low sulphur fuel slips on talk of cargo deals.

text.p: European low sulphur fuel prices slumped on Tuesday on talk of cargo deals into Italy at recent lows and activity in paper markets, traders said.
Swaps fell $2.50 yesterday and lost a further $1 on Tuesday on the back of a rumoured deal into Italy by a Swiss-based trader of 80,000 tonnes of trans-atlantic barrels at $95 cif.
A further cargo deal was rumoured on Tuesday morning, from a French major with British plant, again into Italy.
However neither deal was confirmed and some traders doubted trans-atlantic shipment could be made profitable.
The flurry of activity on the normally dormant low sulphur market was triggered by a surplus of prompt European cargoes, traders said.
The talk left barge business in the shade. Prices slipped slightly, with business again thin. Deals were seen at $81.50 fob in Antwerp and $80 and $81 in Rotterdam.
Prompt high sulphur cargoes were still in short supply in the Mediterranean, propping up prices in the near term.
Talk that 70,000 tonnes of high density, high sulphur cracked was bought at the end of last week from Le Havre by the Swiss-based trader backed the perception of market tightness.
